clue.text: Town fellow following country pursuit

indicators.note: the fellow is placed after the pursuit, as the word following says

parts.note: hunting (with hounds) is the classic pursuit of the English countryside
a don is a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: A man trailing behind a rural sport such as fox-hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: HUNTINGDON is a market town in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Huntingdon is a market town in eastern England, so it is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Woman with common sense, I am bound to be single-minded?

parts.note: Una is a woman's name

indicators.note: the common-sense word is wrapped round the I am contraction, binding it

parts.note: nous is British slang for practical common sense
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: A sensible woman declares she is destined to be focused on one goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of one mind is literally what the Latin roots mean, so a single-minded group is in full agreement; the question mark flags the pun.

clue.text: It could be the future that makes one anxious

definitions.meaning: the future is one of the grammatical forms of a verb, like past and present

explanation.surface: Wondering what lies ahead is what makes a person anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical form of a verb such as the future, and also a word meaning nervously strained.

clue.text: Fish in menu is cooked especially for Pharisee

indicators.note: the fish is placed inside the rearranged letters
cooked means altered or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: cod is a fish

explanation.surface: A diner notes the fish on the menu has been prepared specially for a religious guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns the menu letters into NIEMUS; 'especially for' only links. Nicodemus appears in John's Gospel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicodemus is the Pharisee in John's Gospel who came to Jesus by night.

clue.text: Responsible leader of union ousted in absurd manner

indicators.note: an absurd manner suggests the letters are thrown into a crazy order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A trade union boss is thrown out in a ridiculous way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in absurd manner' rearranges U plus OUSTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Duteous is an old word for dutiful, someone who carries out obligations faithfully.

clue.text: Bottle winner half disposed of before victory

indicators.note: the remaining half comes before the victory letters
one half of the six-letter word winner is got rid of, leaving the other three

parts.note: VE, as in VE Day, stands for Victory in Europe

explanation.surface: A champion knocks back half a bottle ahead of the win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half disposed of' drops WIN from WINNER, leaving NER. VE Day, 8 May 1945, celebrated Victory in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for courage, the same as having the nerve to do something.

clue.text: One attempting to get back a queen, a jack, and a ten

definitions.text: One attempting to get back a queen

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
X is ten in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A card player trying to recover a queen holding a jack and a ten.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a card game, but the queen is Helen of Troy: the Greek hero fought at Troy to win her back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek hero Ajax fought in the Trojan War, which was waged to recover Helen, queen of Sparta.

clue.text: Ban fellow hanging around star

indicators.note: the fellow's name loiters round the ban word, enclosing it

parts.note: Alan is a man's name
to debar is to ban or exclude

explanation.surface: A banned man loiters near a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldebaran is the bright red star marking the eye of Taurus.

clue.text: Portuguese navigator beheaded lizard

indicators.note: beheading a word removes its first letter

parts.note: Vasco da Gama was the Portuguese navigator who sailed to India

explanation.surface: An explorer of old loses his head and is turned into a reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' takes the D off DA GAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: An agama is an Old World lizard of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Good oak cart needed by Highlander

parts.note: a wain is an old word for a farm wagon or cart
a Highlander is a Scot from the Highlands

explanation.surface: A Scotsman needs a sturdy oak cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Wainscot was originally fine imported oak timber used for panelling.

clue.text: Uncomplimentary, reference to Pravda's provocation

definitions.meaning: Pravda was the Soviet Communist newspaper, so a dismissive name for it is a communist rag
something that enrages, as a cloth waved at a bull

explanation.surface: A rude remark about the Soviet newspaper is meant to provoke.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is a contemptuous term for a newspaper, and red means communist.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth waved to enrage a bull, hence anything that infuriates.

clue.text: Essential component of car in grand final

parts.note: grand means big
the final part is the end

explanation.surface: A key car part features in a big final match.
explanation.definitionFit: The big end is the larger end of an engine's connecting rod, round the crankshaft.

clue.text: Be masterful with maiden, perhaps, and simple in speech

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, so it is one kind of over

indicators.note: the word is said out loud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: bare means plain or simple

explanation.surface: Take command of a young woman and speak plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over in cricket is a set of six balls from which no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To overbear is to dominate or domineer, as a masterful person does.

clue.text: Crazy one mustn't be allowed to go off the rails

definitions.meaning: mad, out of one's mind (originally Spanish)

definitions.text: one mustn't be allowed to go off the rails
definitions.meaning: a railway engine must stay on its track; a short form of locomotive

explanation.surface: A mad person must be kept from losing control.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for mad, and also short for a locomotive, a railway engine that must not derail.

clue.text: Working opportunity — time to get stuck in

indicators.note: the time word is lodged inside the opportunity word, as if stuck in it

parts.note: an option is a choice or opportunity
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A job opening means it is time to start working hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Something working is 'in operation': the definition stands for the noun in that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine in operation is functioning, so the noun names the state of running.

clue.text: Popular brand mother's determined to secure

parts.note: ma is mother, so mother's gives ma's

indicators.note: the determined word holds the brand inside it, securing it

parts.note: set means determined, as in set on something
a mark is a brand or trade name

explanation.surface: A mother is set on acquiring a well-known brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods aimed at the general public rather than a niche are for broad consumption.

clue.text: Cowslip, for instance, won't necessarily come out

definitions.text: Cowslip, for instance, won't necessarily come out

parts.words: Cowslip, for instance, won't necessarily come out
parts.note: a cowslip is a plant whose name suggests it blooms in late spring, though it need not open in that month

explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip and hawthorn are both called by a name meaning a bloom of the fifth month.

clue.text: After a shake-up peers exit — the hallmark of meritocracy?

indicators.note: a shake-up rearranges, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Following reform, lords leave the House in a system rewarding ability.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls reform of the House of Lords; 'After a shake-up' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Meritocracy rewards skill and know-how, so specialist skill is its defining mark.

clue.text: Boys enlist when ordered, apparently

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lads sign up for the army when commanded, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seemingly true is true on the face of it, as far as appearances go.

clue.text: Source of berries seen on country walk

definitions.text: Source of berries seen on country walk

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

parts.note: a ramble is a leisurely walk in the countryside

explanation.surface: A blackberry bush spotted on a hike through the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the bush bearing blackberries lines country walks.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackberry bush, a thorny shrub of hedgerows that bears fruit.

clue.text: Negative consequence of gym being closed

parts.note: if the gym is closed there is no gym class, so this gives no
PE, physical education, is the school gym lesson

explanation.surface: The downside of the gym shutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consequence of gym being closed' is no PE; 'consequence of' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A casual, informal way of saying no, a negative reply.

clue.text: Following disorder, a leader very acceptable?

definitions.text: Following disorder, a leader very acceptable?

indicators.note: after disorder the letters are jumbled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: After unrest, a popular national leader emerges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following disorder' rearranges A LEADER plus V. Eamon de Valera led Ireland after the turmoil of the Easter Rising and civil war.
explanation.definitionFit: Eamon de Valera became Irish leader after the troubled years of revolt and civil war, the figure this whole clue paints.

clue.text: Novelist or poet getting endlessly worked up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top, backwards
without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: toiled means worked

explanation.surface: A writer getting endlessly agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TOILED to TOILE; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot was a novelist and T. S. Eliot a poet, so the surname fits both.

clue.text: Heat may be needed for this uniform temperature

definitions.text: Heat may be needed for this

parts.note: even means uniform or level

explanation.surface: Warmth is needed to keep the temperature constant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heat' sounds like warmth, but it is a qualifying race in athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat is a preliminary round, needed when too many competitors enter a race or contest.

clue.text: Passion shown by artist for at least ten years

parts.note: lust is strong passion
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist's desire lasts a decade or more.
explanation.walkthrough: A lustrum is a five-year period, so the plural means two or more of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustra is the plural of lustrum, a period of five years, so two or more make a decade at least.

clue.text: Origin of pigment, 'one found in the drink

definitions.meaning: a brown pigment comes from the ink of the cuttlefish, giving the colour its name
the drink is the sea, and the cuttlefish genus lives there

explanation.surface: Where the colour comes from: something found in a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuttlefish, whose Latin genus name gives its name to the brown ink pigment and which lives in the sea.

clue.text: Delightful nightclub with trendy interior

indicators.note: the trendy word forms the interior of the nightclub word, going inside it

parts.note: a dive is a seedy nightclub or bar
in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: A lovely nightclub with a fashionable decor.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine is used informally to mean heavenly or wonderful.

clue.text: Pole position, at the front

parts.note: a spar projecting forward from a ship's prow is a pole positioned at the very front

explanation.definitionFit: A spar that juts out from the bow of a sailing ship, a pole set at the front.

clue.text: Crazy people about to produce shock

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: nuts are crazy people

explanation.surface: Lunatics on the loose cause alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to daze or astonish, producing a jolt of surprise.

clue.text: Decisive points in court

parts.note: a tennis court, not a law court: a special game of points settling a set level at six games

explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a deciding game is played when a set reaches six games all.
